q: Where does Shewanella oncorhynchi sit relative to S. baltica and S. putrefaciens if you reconcile pangenome-, 16S-, and ANI-based species delimitation? Z-P2 is <95% ANI to all 10 S. putrefaciens comparators (fastANI top hit YZ08 = 91.25% here; paper 90.09%), which supports the S. oncorhynchi novel-species claim by the ANI criterion, but this replication did NOT independently compute 16S rRNA identity or dDDH vs Shewanella type strains, and the closest neighbor in the paper's comparator set is S. putrefaciens YZ08 (a strain historically confused with S. baltica). It is therefore unresolved whether all three axes (pangenome tree topology / 16S identity / whole-genome ANI/dDDH) agree on the species boundary, or whether S. oncorhynchi, S. baltica, and S. putrefaciens form a semi-continuous complex where 16S is too conserved to separate them and pan-genome clustering is threshold-sensitive.
basis: REPORT.md §4.5 (fastANI 91.25% vs YZ08; paper 90.09%; all comparators <95% species boundary), REPORT.md §4.4 (pan-genome cluster count reproduces within ~1% at 70% id; Z-P2 unique 531 vs 618 = ~14% gap), REPORT.md Critique (§Genuine Critique: no 16S rRNA identity or dDDH computed vs Shewanella type strains; species boundary accepted from paper).
next_steps: 1) Extract Z-P2 16S rRNA sequences from the RefSeq GFF (already annotated: 10×16S copies) and BLAST against S. baltica, S. putrefaciens, S. oncorhynchi type-strain 16S; report min/mean/max identity. 2) Run GGDC/dDDH (Type Strain Genome Server) with Z-P2 vs S. baltica type, S. putrefaciens type, and S. oncorhynchi type; the 70% dDDH threshold is the classical species boundary. 3) Build a core-gene phylogeny (Roary core alignment → IQ-TREE) on Z-P2 + 10 S. putrefaciens + S. baltica type + S. oncorhynchi type + 5 additional Shewanella species to see whether the three-axis (pan-tree / 16S / ANI-dDDH) verdicts agree.

q: Does Z-P2 carry a salmon/trout-specific pathogenicity or host-tropism gene repertoire distinct from environmental (crayfish/seawater/sediment) Shewanella? The species name 'oncorhynchi' points at salmonids (genus Oncorhynchus), yet Z-P2 was isolated from spoiled vacuum-packed crayfish in Hubei, China. The paper's claimed 30 virulence genes (>70% id) were not re-run here (C7 not tested), so the actual host-tropism-relevant gene repertoire — adhesins, T3SS/T6SS effectors, hemolysins, iron-piracy systems beyond putrebactin — remains uncatalogued in this replication, and whether Z-P2 encodes fish-mucosal-tropism factors versus generic environmental colonization factors is open.
basis: REPORT.md §1 (Z-P2 isolated from spoiled vacuum-packed crayfish, not fish), REPORT.md §2/§4.6 (C7 virulence genes not re-run; would require VFDB BLAST), REPORT.md §4.3 (putrebactin siderophore + TonB-dependent receptor confirmed = iron acquisition system present, but broader virulence/host-tropism repertoire not enumerated).
next_steps: 1) BLAST Z-P2 protein.faa vs VFDB core dataset at ≥70% id / ≥70% coverage; classify hits by virulence category (adhesion, secretion system, toxin, iron acquisition, immune evasion). 2) Cross-reference against Shewanella-specific fish-pathogen VFs from S. algae, S. baltica fish-farm isolates, and S. anguillimortifera literature. 3) Comparative VF profile: same VFDB BLAST against the 10 S. putrefaciens comparators + published S. oncorhynchi salmon-associated isolates (if any in RefSeq); tabulate presence/absence to identify Z-P2-unique or S. oncorhynchi-clade-enriched VFs. 4) Scan for known fish-mucin-binding lectins and salmonid-specific adhesin motifs.

q: Does Z-P2 carry a cold-water aquaculture / psychrophilic-adaptation gene signature, and if so is it S. oncorhynchi-lineage-specific or convergent across cold-adapted Shewanella? Cold-adaptation signatures typically include cold-shock proteins (CspA family expansions), fatty-acid desaturases, EPA/DHA biosynthesis clusters (Pfa), RNA-helicases (DeaD/CsdA), compatible-solute transporters, and anti-freeze-associated genes. This replication confirmed the EPA (hglE-KS / Pfa) cluster at 3,385,779–3,403,945 (marker enzymes PfaD, PfaB, phosphopantetheine-binding protein, hotdog thioesterase — a definitive Pfa cluster), which is a strong psychrophilic-membrane-fluidity signal. But no CspA family census, no desaturase inventory, and no core-vs-accessory placement of these genes in the 11-genome pan-genome was done, so whether Z-P2's cold-adaptation cassette is a shared Shewanella-clade feature or an S. oncorhynchi-enriched signature is open.
basis: REPORT.md §4.3 (EPA/Pfa cluster verified at 3,385,779–3,403,945 with PfaD + PfaB + PPant-binding + hotdog thioesterase = definitive Pfa cluster), REPORT.md §4.4 (pan-genome Z-P2 unique = 531 clusters at 70% id — the accessory-vs-unique partition is available but not functionally annotated here).
next_steps: 1) HMMER search Z-P2 protein.faa against Pfam CSD (cold-shock domain) and DEAD-box RNA-helicase HMMs; count paralogs and compare to the 10 comparators. 2) BLAST fatty-acid desaturase families (des-like) across all 11 genomes; map presence to a core/accessory partition of the Roary output. 3) Cross-check the Pfa cluster synteny and gene identity across all 11 Shewanella genomes to test whether it is core-conserved or Z-P2/S. oncorhynchi-enriched. 4) COG/KEGG functional enrichment on the 531 Z-P2-unique gene clusters — look for over-representation of cold-response, membrane-lipid, and osmoprotection categories.

q: How variable are Z-P2's TMAO-reductase (TorA/TorC/DmsA) and dissimilatory Fe(III)-reductase (MtrABC/OmcA/CymA — the Shewanella-hallmark decaheme cytochrome pathway) operons across the 11-genome pan-genome, and do they co-vary with biofilm/salmon-mucus colonization capacity? These are the classical Shewanella respiratory hallmarks and directly relevant to salmonid-mucus and post-harvest low-oxygen environments, yet this replication did not inventory them: the pan-genome analysis (§4.4) produced cluster counts but no functional categorization of the core-vs-accessory partition. Whether these operons are strictly core (shared by all 11) or accessory/variable is unresolved.
basis: REPORT.md §4.4 (Roary @70%: 2656 core, 9332 pan clusters — but no functional annotation of core/accessory partition), REPORT.md §4.3 (only the 5 antiSMASH BGCs verified; broader respiratory/electron-transfer operons not scanned), REPORT.md §1 (Z-P2 isolated from spoiled vacuum-packed crayfish = low-oxygen/TMAO-rich environment where these pathways matter).
next_steps: 1) BLAST Shewanella oneidensis MR-1 reference TMAO-reductase (TorA, TorC, TorR) and Mtr pathway (MtrA/MtrB/MtrC/OmcA/CymA) protein sequences against all 11 genomes; report identity/coverage and operon synteny. 2) Map the hits onto Roary's gene_presence_absence matrix — are they in the 2656 core, in the accessory shell, or Z-P2-unique? 3) Cross-reference with biofilm-formation loci (bpfA-like, exopolysaccharide biosynthesis clusters); test co-occurrence via Fisher's exact / phi-coefficient on the Roary matrix. 4) Where operon variability is found, examine flanking regions for mobility markers (IS elements, integrases) to test whether the variability is HGT-driven.

q: What is the Shewanella-mediated seafood-spoilage risk-gene inventory for salmonid post-harvest, and where does Z-P2 sit on it? Spoilage-relevant gene categories include TMAO reductase (fish-off-odor precursor), biogenic amine decarboxylases (histidine decarboxylase = histamine/scombroid poisoning; ornithine/lysine decarboxylases = putrescine/cadaverine — note ornithine is also the putrebactin precursor here), sulfide-producing cysteine desulfhydrases, and proteolytic/lipolytic enzyme repertoires. Z-P2 was isolated from spoiled crayfish and demonstrably produces the ornithine-derived siderophore putrebactin (ornithine N5-oxygenase + IucA/IucC verified at 1,858,771–1,862,960), so its ornithine metabolism is measurably active — but a systematic spoilage-risk gene inventory across the 11-genome pan-genome, ranked by salmonid post-harvest relevance, was not built. Whether Z-P2 poses a high, medium, or low seafood-spoilage-risk profile relative to comparator S. putrefaciens strains is unresolved.
basis: REPORT.md §1 (Z-P2 isolated from spoiled vacuum-packed crayfish — direct seafood-spoilage provenance), REPORT.md §4.3 (putrebactin NIS operon with ornithine N5-oxygenase + IucA/IucC verified — confirms active ornithine-hydroxamate metabolism), REPORT.md §4.4 (pan-genome cluster counts done but not functionally categorized for spoilage-relevant gene families), REPORT.md §4.6 (C7 virulence/CRISPR not re-run — spoilage-risk repertoire similarly not inventoried).
next_steps: 1) Curate a salmonid-post-harvest spoilage-risk gene panel: TMAO reductase (TorA/DmsA), histidine decarboxylase (hdc), ornithine/lysine decarboxylases (odc/ldc), agmatinase, cysteine desulfhydrases, extracellular proteases (Prt-family), lipases (Lip-family), chitinases. 2) BLAST panel against all 11 genomes at ≥50% id / ≥70% cov; build a spoilage-risk heatmap ranking Z-P2 vs S. putrefaciens comparators. 3) Cross-reference biogenic-amine decarboxylase hits with Roary accessory-vs-core placement to test whether the spoilage risk is a clade-conserved core or a strain-variable accessory feature. 4) In-silico predict cold-active spoilage protease/lipase activity by combining hit list with the psychrophilic-adaptation panel from Q3.
